newsitem.title: USA: Court approves California deal with calcium makers.
newsitem.headline: Court approves California deal with calcium makers.

text.p: A California court Monday upheld the state's settlement with eight leading manufacturers of calcium supplements and antacids to reduce lead levels in their products, the companies said.

The settlement, announced in April by the state's attorney general, resolved a dispute over California's Proposition 65, a state law which requires consumer warnings when toxic chemical exposure exceeds safety standards. Lead has been linked to brain damage and birth defects.
The non-profit environmental group Natural Resources Defense Council opposed the deal, warning that the state's settlement would not go far enough to reduce lead levels.
Despite the opposition, a Superior Court judge upheld the settlement Monday, the manufacturers said in a statement. A copy of the decision was not immediately available.

"We are pleased with today's decision to uphold the California attorney general's settlement regarding lead levels in calcium supplements," said Roger Carrick, a spokesman for the Association for Responsible Calcium Products, which represented calcium supplement and antacid manufacturers.

As part of the agreement, the calcium industry will reduce naturally-occurring lead levels. The settlement called for further reductions in lead over the next two years for calcium supplements and antacid products.

The settlement was reached with: SmithKline Beecham Consumer Healthcare, a unit of SmithKline Beecham Plc; Warner-Lambert Co.; American Home Products Corp.; Pharmavite Corp.; General Nutrition Corp.; Perrigo Co.; Schering-Plough Health Care Products Inc.; and Twin Laboratories.
